problem: According to the rational roots theorem, which of the following could be a root of the polynomial $f(x)=8{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+10?$

feedback.problem: According to the rational roots theorem, which of the following could be a root of the polynomial $f(x)=3{x}^{3}+x-6?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a polynomial with integer coefficients, the rational roots theorem states that any rational roots of the polynomial must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of the constant term}}{\text{factor of the leading coefficient}}.
$$

For the given polynomial $f(x),$ the constant term is $-6,$ and the leading coefficient is $3.$ So, any rational roots of $f(x)$ must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of }-6}{\text{factor of }3}.
$$

Of the given answer choices, only $\frac{2}{3}$ takes the above form since the numerator $(2)$ is a factor of $-6$ and the denominator $(3)$ is a factor of $3.$
